label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa contra gentiles I.2…… supports A move that affirms that God can be known…
note: SCG I.2 n.4 names natural reason as that 'cui omnes assentire coguntur', invoked against Muslims and pagans, who share no scriptural authority with Christians: scholastic usage of natural reason as reason shared with outsiders to Christianity. Gaps: whether the pagans meant are outside every theological horizon is not stated (a further bridge); and Aquinas is a theologian of the practice, not its council, so that Vatican I's 'naturali humanae rationis lumine' has his sense is a reading step.
